I upvoted because I think that content consumption by type SHOULD be left to users. Additionally, the platform is pro-creator and has been since 2015. However, I wonder how much it will really matter to the greater public when/if tagging for AI content does get added. I can already envision slopworlds becoming prevalent and people joining those just for that appeal, alone. Tagging and sorting by AI might actually end up doing more harm in regards to traffic movement on the platform. I'm not sure if you all remember but there was a trend about 7 or 8 years ago where world builders would just spaghetti up a world as much as possible and people would go in there just to see what's broken. To me, making joke worlds is just as harmful to creator promotion as AI would be because it draws traffic from genuine art and hobbyists, but I digress.

I also worry about where people will not draw their line. I would be remiss to not mention that there is already a lot of vibe coding cooked into the worlds you all already know and love. Should those be tagged as AI as well? Since this pulls from known coding languages and translates it into a workable code, is this excusable? What if it isn't? How would you tell? How do you police failure to tag? 

I just don't see great answers to the above questions.

VRChat may very well respond to your request but I don't think it will have the social outcome you'd prefer to see. It would be a very small, negligible, almost ignorable change.

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/filters-for-ai-generated-content

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/tackle-the-misleading-world-thumbnails-issue

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/add-contains-generative-ai-content-tag-to-the-content-gating-system

https://feedback.vrchat.com/feature-requests/p/require-content-using-generative-ai-to-declare-it

How many more posts is it going to take before the devs start to acknowledge this.

I've absolutely had it now with VRChat and generative lie machines and asset imitation. DO. SOMETHING. NOW. I will no longer be exploring worlds made or updated after September 3rd, 2026 unless it's a user I trust or until SOMETHING is done!

If VRChat doesn't do something by the end of the month, I may actually just stop using VRChat entirely as clearly the feedback website is just a hole to yell into for the devs to ignore. This is ridiculous. I CAN'T TAKE IT ANYMORE!

Mildly disturbing this is an issue to such an extent. Vibe coded world assets are already kind of common, so seeing it become fully automated makes me feel kind of dirty if I'm honest.

I do hope the devs take this into consideration.

Fuck AI. Can't believe these programs intended to exterminate humanity are allowed in any way to be involved with VRchat. LLMs are based on theft, and ought to be deleted and have the plugs pulled on them.

This is entirely unacceptable that VRC has let this go unnoticed for this long. AI usage is already a problem: world assets, models and textures. 

As someone else in this thread mentioned: how many cannies is this going to take before VRChat does something? How many creators have to leave the platform before VRChat gives a shit? 

In all honesty, at this point we need to start voting with our wallets. If VRChat isn't going to listen to the cannies, then maybe cancelling VRC+ and refusing to purchase anything at the shop will get them to listen.

Any AI content should just be outright banned. No need for a title or label or tag. 

People have Brains to be creative. Use that instead.
ALL genAI needs to be just straight up banned from VRC, and the fact they don't seem to care is disgusting. VRC is meant to be for HUMAN creators, not slop machines.

details:
Just today I have seen 3 X/Twitter posts of fully AI generated worlds made using GPT-6 Astra, one of them already published.

https://x.com/yuipxq/status/2097025460295389601

https://x.com/kurotori4423/status/2097011323767034098

https://x.com/pichikyo/status/2096285284178788612

I fear this kind of content will soon flood the platform. VRChat needed to add some kind of AI tag or descriptor a long time ago. This kind of quickly and effortlessly generated content hurts existing creators on this platform.

Please don't let this become another "too little, too late" situation. VRChat needs an identifier for AI generated content added ASAP. Regardless of how end users personally feel about the use of AI, a way to separate and identify AI generated content from user created content is an absolute necessity.
title: Add an AI content identifier for worlds and avatars
